subagent_reports.architecture_assessment: Decision 3 resolves prior blocker 1: for policy-derived blockable tools, only non-null callerSessionID equal to non-null mainSessionId is allowed; sub-agent, missing-caller, and unresolved-baseline cases block. Union-floor tools are disjoint from the valid complement by construction, so they do not reopen blockable tools; this satisfies AC5/AC8/C5 (adv_change_show://gateAgentToolsRole?include=agreement,design; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/tool-role-policy.ts). Decision 4 resolves prior blocker 2: RoleFirewallError with stable code ROLE_FIREWALL_BLOCK plus tool/reason/resolution is adequate, and upstream awaits the before hook before tool execution (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/453b61e27b2f6c2752a60dd7d8412bdcf4e0aa3d/packages/opencode/src/session/tools.ts#L75-L130). Decision 6 closes roster drift: current assets contain nine mode:subagent manifests; positive two-way parity plus required policy rows catches additions/removals (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/tree/main/.opencode/agents; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/tool-role-policy.ts). Proposed explicit workflow-reachability assertion is adequate because the test walks static imports transitively from workflows.ts (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/temporal/workflow-bundle-boundary.test.ts). Prior blocker 3 remains: Decision 5 says static AGENT_TOOL_POLICY import failure delegates to createDegradedToolMap, but AdvancePlugin's try/catch can run only after index.ts and static dependencies load. Static dependency evaluation precedes importing-module body, so failure bypasses that wrapper (https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/import; https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/index.ts#L1257-L1283). New nonblocking wording defect: Decision 2 says every mutation is blockable, but intentional union-floor evidence/report writes include adv_wisdom_add and adv_subagent_report_submit; narrow wording to orchestration/authority mutations (https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/tool-role-policy.ts#L622-L803).

blockers: Decision 5 still fails AC8/C5 as written: static tool-role-policy load/evaluation failure occurs before index.ts's factory wrapper can execute, so that path cannot return createDegradedToolMap. Sources: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Statements/import and https://github.com/Sharper-Flow/Advance/blob/main/plugin/src/index.ts#L1257-L1283.
validation.notes: Prior blockers 1 and 2 resolved. Prior blocker 3 remains. Decision 6 and explicit workflow-bundle non-reachability test adequately close earlier roster and bundle gaps.

tradeoffs: Fail-closed unresolved-role handling may transiently reject a legitimate pre-baseline main-session authority call, but preserves orientation reads and prevents silent privilege expansion.
Generated manifests plus coarse runtime firewall add policy/test maintenance, but provide defense in depth.
Catchable module-load recovery may require runtime loading indirection; static imports remain simpler but cannot promise degraded recovery from dependency load/evaluation failure.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Factory-local try/catch cannot catch failure that prevents index.ts evaluation.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Preserves AC8/C5; dynamic-import load/evaluation rejection is catchable per MDN.

alternatives_considered.rationale: Simpler, but changes approved contract and needs orchestrator/user agreement.

# Proposal

## Why

ADV registers all **80** agent-callable `adv_*` tools as one flat top-level map at the plugin SDK boundary (`ADV_PUBLIC_TOOL_BASELINE_COUNT = 80`). Per-agent exposure is applied downstream by OpenCode's permission layer reading each agent's `tools:` YAML frontmatter. `tool-role-policy.ts` classifies authority into three classes — `orchestrator` (63), `operator-only` (9), `dual` (8) — and `tool-role-policy.test.ts` enforces manifest↔policy parity (including "operator-only tools grantable only to `adv`"). But that policy is advisory/audit-time: **no plugin runtime consumer reads it**, and manifests are hand-maintained and only checked, not generated.

## Outcome

Make role-scoped exposure structural on two ADV-owned surfaces, without modifying OpenCode:

1. **Generated manifests (fine-grained, drift-free).** Treat `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` as the single source of truth and *generate* each agent's `tools:` YAML block from it at build/deploy time, so per-lane exposure cannot drift from policy. The existing parity test becomes a generate-and-verify check.

2. **Runtime fail-closed backstop (coarse, security-critical).** Add a guard in the plugin's existing `tool.execute.before` hook: when a call targets an `operator-only` or `orchestrator`-class tool from a **sub-agent session** (`callerSessionID !== mainSessionId`), throw to block it — mirroring the shipped Trunk Write Firewall block pattern. This holds even if a manifest is wrong or the model is prompted to call the tool.

## Authority model

No user authentication and no model-reported identity. The SDK `tool.execute.before` hook exposes `{tool, sessionID, callID}` only — so runtime role is bound to the **trusted session distinction** (orchestrator/main session vs sub-agent session), the same signal already used for sub-agent spawn accounting and main-session `todowrite` projection. Existing `approvedByUser`, approval-evidence, permission, and operator checks remain the mutation authority; role exposure is an added least-privilege boundary.

## Scope

- Generate each agent's `tools:` manifest block from `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY`; convert the parity test to generate-and-verify.
- Add a plugin `tool.execute.before` fail-closed guard blocking `operator-only` and `orchestrator`-class tools from sub-agent sessions.
- Define fail-closed behavior for unknown tools, unknown/unclassified policy rows, and missing/failed policy load (degrade to safe-diagnostic exposure, never the full surface).
- Preserve explicit orchestrator (main-session) access to the tools needed to drive the seven-gate lifecycle.
- Add tests: policy/inventory coverage, generated-manifest parity, sub-agent-session block (operator-only + orchestrator), main-session allow, spoofing resistance (forged args cannot elevate), and degraded-mode.

## Acceptance direction

- Every registered tool has exactly one machine-checkable role policy row, and every agent manifest `tools:` block is generated from it (CI fails on drift or unclassified tools).
- An operator-only or orchestrator-only tool call from a sub-agent session is blocked at runtime regardless of manifest contents or prompt text.
- Main/orchestrator-session calls to owned tools behave exactly as today, with audit metadata unchanged.
- Policy-load or role-resolution failure yields a typed degraded catalog of safe diagnostics; it never falls back to the full tool surface and never mutates workflow state.

## Boundaries / avoidances

- Do not modify OpenCode core; use only ADV-owned agent assets and the plugin's own hook.
- Do not consolidate semantically distinct repair/promotion/lifecycle tools solely to reduce count.
- Do not encode authority in prompt descriptions alone, or trust model prose / caller-supplied role parameters as identity.
- Do not attempt runtime per-lane (engineer vs designer) discrimination — the SDK hook has no agent identity; per-lane gating stays in the generated-manifest permission layer.
- Do not depend on OpenCode Code Mode or the proposed MCP read surface (Epic entry 4).

# Problem Statement

## Who / What

ADV registers all 80 agent-callable `adv_*` tools as one flat top-level map at the plugin SDK boundary. Which tools each agent may actually call is decided downstream by OpenCode's permission layer reading each agent's hand-maintained `tools:` YAML frontmatter. `tool-role-policy.ts` classifies every tool (`orchestrator` 63, `operator-only` 9, `dual` 8) and CI parity tests assert the manifests match that policy — but the policy is advisory/audit-time only, with no plugin runtime consumer.

## Why it matters

Two structural weaknesses remain:

1. **Drift risk.** Agent manifests are authored by hand and only *checked* against `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY`. The source of truth (policy) and the enforced artifact (manifest YAML) are maintained separately, so they can diverge until CI catches it — and only for cases the parity test covers.

2. **No runtime backstop.** If a manifest were wrong, or a sub-agent were prompt-injected, nothing inside the plugin prevents an operator-only or orchestrator-only tool from executing. The only enforcement is the manifest the plugin itself does not verify at call time.

## Desired outcome

- Agent tool exposure is derived from a single machine-checkable policy rather than parallel-maintained YAML that can drift.
- Operator-only and orchestrator-only tools cannot execute from a sub-agent session even if a manifest is wrong or the model is prompted to call them.
- All of this is achieved within ADV-owned surfaces (plugin hook + generated agent assets); OpenCode core is not modified.

## Constraints surfaced during investigation

- The OpenCode plugin SDK `tool.execute.before` hook input is `{tool, sessionID, callID}` — no agent identity. Runtime role can only be bound to the trusted session distinction (orchestrator/main session vs sub-agent session), never to model-reported identity or prompt text.
- Fine-grained per-lane exposure (engineer vs designer vs reviewer) remains the responsibility of OpenCode's permission layer; the plugin runtime can only enforce the coarse operator-only/orchestrator-only-from-subagent boundary.
- Mutation authority (`approvedByUser`, approval-evidence, operator checks) is unchanged; role exposure is an added least-privilege boundary, not a replacement.

# Design (rev 3 — validation-clean)

## Architecture overview

Two independent, ADV-owned mechanisms sharing one source of truth (`AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` in `plugin/src/tool-role-policy.ts`):

1. **Build-time manifest generator** → writes each agent's `tools:` YAML block.
2. **Runtime session firewall** → blocks non-union `adv_*` tools from sub-agent (and role-unresolved) sessions in the plugin's existing `tool.execute.before` hook.

No workflow-reachable code changes; no Temporal surface; no OpenCode core changes.

## Decision 1 — Manifest generation (marker-bounded block, not full-file)

- New `plugin/scripts/generate-agent-manifests.ts`: reads `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY`, and for each shipped agent rewrites only the `tools:` frontmatter block of `.opencode/agents/<agent>.md` between exactly one sentinel-marker pair inside the frontmatter `tools:` mapping. Agent prose/body and all bytes outside the marker pair are preserved.
- Emission order encodes OpenCode last-match-wins: built-in tool lines (hand-owned, above the marker), then `adv_*: false` deny wildcard (when `denyWildcard`), then explicit `adv_x: true` grants (sorted allowlist), then explicit `adv_x: false` (sorted `explicitBlocked`). The orchestrator (`adv`, no wildcard) emits its full explicit grant list.
- Structural guards (all CI-tested): exactly one marker pair per file; missing/duplicate markers fail; byte preservation outside markers; idempotent round trip (generate∘generate == generate); emitted block parses as valid YAML; first-run baseline normalization so committed manifests round-trip exactly.
- `pnpm run generate:manifests` (write) and `generate:manifests --check` (verify, non-zero on drift) are added; `--check` joins `pnpm run check`; the writer runs in `deploy-local.sh --fix` before agent sync.
- The existing `tool-role-policy.test.ts` manifest-exactness block is retargeted to assert `generated === committed` for every agent (AC2/AC3). The registry-parity invariant (a registered tool with no policy row fails CI) is preserved unchanged.

Rejected alternative: whole-file generation — agent `.md` bodies are hand-authored instruction prose; generating them would destroy authored content.

## Decision 2 — Runtime blockable set derived from policy (not class)

- Pure helpers in `tool-role-policy.ts`: `subAgentUnionAllowlist()` = union of `allowed` across the spawnable sub-agent roster (Decision 6); `blockableFromSubAgentSession()` = `ADV_TOOL_NAMES \ union`.
- Consequence (verified): union floor = `adv_change_list/show, adv_gate_status, adv_project_context, adv_run_test, adv_snapshot_health, adv_spec, adv_status, adv_subagent_report_submit, adv_task_list/ready/show, adv_wisdom_add/list, adv_session_list, adv_temporal_diagnose, adv_wip_state` — note this intentionally includes evidence/report writes (`adv_wisdom_add`, `adv_subagent_report_submit`). All 9 operator-only tools and every **orchestration/authority mutation, gate, epic, and worktree** tool are blockable. Satisfies DONT1.

## Decision 3 — Session-role resolution: FAIL-CLOSED when unresolved

- Runtime role uses only `input.sessionID` vs the plugin's captured `mainSessionId` (existing capture at first `experimental.chat.system.transform`).
- **Enforcement predicate (fail-closed):** for an `adv_*` tool in `blockableFromSubAgentSession`, ALLOW only when `mainSessionId != null && callerSessionID != null && callerSessionID === mainSessionId`. In every other case — sub-agent session, `mainSessionId` unresolved, or `callerSessionID` missing — BLOCK. Aligns with AC8/C5.
- **Cost analysis (accepted):** the only calls blocked in the pre-baseline window are *blockable* tools (orchestration/authority mutations, operator, gate, epic, worktree). Union-floor reads remain allowed regardless of baseline, so main-session orientation is never blocked. In normal OpenCode ordering the main session's `chat.system.transform` sets `mainSessionId` before its first tool call; if a rare ordering delays baseline, a blocked call surfaces a typed, retryable error rather than a silent fail-open. No documented lifecycle invariant is relied upon.

## Decision 4 — Firewall placement, typed error, coexistence

- Add `roleFirewallCheck` at the top of `handleToolExecuteBefore`, adjacent to the trunk-write firewall, evaluated only for `adv_*` tool names.
- On block it throws a typed `RoleFirewallError` (stable `code: "ROLE_FIREWALL_BLOCK"`, `tool`, `reason`, `resolution: "sub_agent" | "unresolved_role"`) whose message begins `Role firewall:`. Throwing aborts the tool call: verified in upstream OpenCode that the custom-tool executor awaits `tool.execute.before` and the plugin trigger does not swallow rejections, so this covers `adv_*` tools, not only built-ins.
- It returns/no-ops for non-`adv_*` tools, union-floor tools, and confirmed main-session calls — so the existing `task`, `question`, `todowrite`, adv_* re-point, and reachability branches run unchanged for the main session. C3 coexistence is asserted by an integration test.

## Decision 5 — Fail-closed scope: runtime failure only (static integrity is a CI-time guarantee)

- **Scope (user-approved Option A):** AC8/C5 fail-closed governs *runtime* failure — computing the blockable set from the loaded policy and resolving session role. If `blockableFromSubAgentSession()` throws or yields an empty/invalid set at runtime, the firewall treats the union floor as the only sub-agent-allowed set and blocks everything else from non-main sessions; exposure failure never mutates workflow state and never falls back to the full surface.
- **Static module-load integrity is out of the runtime envelope.** `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` is a compile-time constant via static import; an ES-module evaluation failure fails the entire plugin load (true of every static import) and is prevented at build/CI time by typecheck + tests — it is not a runtime-recoverable condition and is deliberately not handled by the hook. No dynamic import is introduced for a CI-prevented failure mode (avoids an anti-pattern async init path around a compile-time constant).

## Decision 6 — Authoritative positive spawnable-roster parity

- Add a shared exported constant `SPAWNABLE_SUBAGENT_ROSTER` (the nine `mode: subagent` agents) used by `subAgentUnionAllowlist()`.
- New parity test parses every `.opencode/agents/*.md` frontmatter `mode` and asserts the set of `mode: subagent` agents equals `SPAWNABLE_SUBAGENT_ROSTER`, and that each roster agent has an `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` row. Two-way parity upgrades the existing phantom (negative) roster test, so adding/removing a sub-agent without updating the roster fails CI (mitigates over-block drift, R2).

## Spoofing resistance (AC7)

Role is a function of `sessionID` only; no code path reads a caller-supplied role/argument to grant exposure. A forged arg (e.g. `role: "orchestrator"`) is ignored. Test asserts a sub-agent-session call carrying forged args is still blocked.

## Test plan (AC9)

- Unit: `subAgentUnionAllowlist` / `blockableFromSubAgentSession` derivation; `SPAWNABLE_SUBAGENT_ROSTER` positive parity; generator determinism, idempotent round trip, single-marker/duplicate/missing-marker failure, byte preservation, YAML validity; generate-and-verify `--check`.
- Hook: sub-agent-session block for representative operator-only (`adv_change_workflow_terminate`) and orchestrator-only (`adv_gate_complete`) tools; sub-agent-session allow for union tools (`adv_run_test`, `adv_subagent_report_submit`); main-session allow of a blockable tool; unresolved-baseline BLOCK of a blockable tool + unresolved-baseline ALLOW of a union read; fail-closed derivation; spoofing resistance; typed `RoleFirewallError` shape.
- Coexistence: extend `integration.test.ts` so trunk-write firewall, reachability gate, spawn accounting, and todowrite projection tests pass with the role firewall active.
- Boundary: explicit assertion that `tool-role-policy.ts` remains outside the Temporal workflow bundle import graph (`workflow-bundle-boundary.test.ts`).
- Full: `pnpm run check`, build, `bin/oc-test full` (AC10).

## Risks

- R1: Sentinel-marker generation must round-trip existing manifests exactly on first run; mitigated by a normalization pass + committing the generated baseline in this change, plus idempotence tests.
- R2: Roster drift (new sub-agent added without allowlist) would over-block; mitigated by the Decision 6 positive-roster parity test failing CI on mismatch.
- R3: If OpenCode changes sub-agent session semantics, the coarse backstop could mis-scope; mitigated by keeping fine-grained gating in generated manifests (defense in depth) and documenting the SDK dependency inline.
- R4: Fail-closed pre-baseline could block a legitimate main-session mutation under abnormal hook ordering; bounded by union-floor reads always allowed and a typed retryable error; no silent fail-open.

# Executive Summary

## Outcome

ADV agent tool exposure is now structurally role-scoped from a single source of truth (`AGENT_TOOL_POLICY`), enforced on two ADV-owned layers with no OpenCode core modification.

## Value

Operator-only and orchestrator-only tools can no longer reach a sub-agent — even if an agent manifest drifts or a sub-agent is prompt-injected. Agent manifests can no longer silently diverge from policy. Least-privilege tool exposure becomes machine-checkable rather than hand-maintained.

## Delivered

- **Generated manifests (fine-grained):** `generate-agent-manifests.ts` emits each agent's `adv_*` `tools:` block from `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` between sentinel markers, preserving hand-owned non-adv lines. `generate:manifests:check` (in `pnpm run check`) fails CI on any drift, including dropped non-adv grants. Wired into `deploy-local.sh --fix` (non-fatal).
- **Runtime session firewall (coarse backstop):** typed `RoleFirewallError` + fail-closed `roleFirewallCheck` at the top of `tool.execute.before`. A blockable `adv_*` tool (anything outside the sub-agent union floor) is allowed only from the confirmed main/orchestrator session; sub-agent and role-unresolved sessions are blocked. Role binds to `sessionID` only.
- **Policy helpers:** `SPAWNABLE_SUBAGENT_ROSTER`, `subAgentUnionAllowlist()`, `blockableFromSubAgentSession()` with positive two-way roster parity; `tool-role-policy.ts` kept out of the Temporal workflow bundle.

## Verification

- Acceptance reviewer: READY, no scoped fixes required.
- Runtime firewall: 21 tests (block/allow/unresolved/spoofing/typed-error).
- Coexistence: 113 tests — trunk-write firewall, reachability gate, spawn accounting, todowrite projection unchanged.
- Generator: determinism, idempotence, marker structural guards, generated==committed; asset clusters 101, overlay-sync 21.
- `pnpm run check` (incl `generate:manifests:check`) + `pnpm run build` green. Zero deterministic SEMANTIC failures.
- Contract review matrix: 28/28 passing/respected/not-applicable.

## Design decisions of note

- Runtime backstop is derived from `AGENT_TOOL_POLICY` union-complement, **not** the tool-role class — workers legitimately call orchestrator-class tools like `adv_run_test`, so class-based blocking would break them.
- Fail-closed when session role is unresolved (validator-corrected from an initial fail-open draft).
- AC8/C5 fail-closed scopes to runtime derivation/role failure; static module-load integrity stays a CI-time guarantee (no dynamic-import anti-pattern) — user-approved.

## Risks / follow-ups

- **AC10 full-suite:** local `bin/oc-test full` was blocked by an external shared full-tier lock (unrelated worktrees); deterministic surface is green. CI's isolated full run on the PR is the authoritative AC10 verdict at release (user-approved).
- Nonblocking: harden the deploy generate-step failure handling (reviewer suggestion) — candidate fast-follow.
- Fine-grained per-lane exposure remains OpenCode-manifest-enforced; the runtime backstop is intentionally coarse (session-role only).
